subject: Aligning demo timing with trace review & travel
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jo <emma.jo@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-27 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning demo timing with trace review & travel

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for setting up the showcase week. A couple of constraints came up on our side and I wanted to propose a small shift so both teams get the prep we need and your execs aren’t inconvenienced by travel.

High-level ask:
- Move the public demo so your exec-level stakeholders can attend post-travel (we understand they’re traveling end of this week).
- Add a short internal dry-run 24–48 hours before the customer-facing session so we can validate prompt sets, run through workload traces, and confirm sample data ingestion.

Why: the demo relies on your sanitized sample dataset and a short prompt QA pass to ensure we don’t hit regressions during the live session. We also need a couple of permission items from FinLytics so our engineer can ingest and validate traces in the dedicated demo environment.

Proposed options (all PT):
- Option A: Customer demo — Thu, May 7 at 10:00am; Internal dry-run — Wed, May 6 at 3:00pm
- Option B: Customer demo — Mon, May 11 at 11:00am; Internal dry-run — Fri, May 8 at 2:00pm

Pre-demo checklist (what we need from FinLytics before the internal dry-run):
- A sanitized sample CSV (column names and expected row counts) or Drive link to upload (we can accept S3/Drive).
- A service account (or temporary credentials) with read-only access to the sample location for ingestion.
- Any workload traces you can share (sample latency/throughput traces) — a small trace_v1.json is ideal.
- Confirmation of exec attendance window so we don’t schedule during travel.

I attached a short sample_requirements.md that outlines the preferred schema and file sizes. Ben and Marissa will join the prep and run the dry-run. Please tell us which option works and whether you prefer hosted-demo or an on-prem walkthrough.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: sample_requirements.md (text)
From: Emma Jo <emma.jo@finlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: support@finlytics.com
Date: 2026-04-27 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning demo timing with trace review & travel

Monica —

Appreciate the heads-up. Execs are on a customer site through Apr 30–May 2 and returning late May 6, so Option A (May 7) looks better for the execs. May 11 is also possible but several folks will be out the following week.

We can provide a sanitized CSV and don’t have S3 access configured for vendors yet — I’ll upload the file to a shared Google Drive folder and send the link once it’s ready. I’ve looped our ops alias (support@finlytics.com) for permissioning and to coordinate the temporary service account.

One question: can your team complete the prompt validation without the full trace set, or do you need the workload traces prior to the internal dry-run? If the latter, we’ll prioritize extracting a small trace sample today.

Thanks —
Emma
Head of Product Operations | FinLytics
emma.jo@finlytics.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jo <emma.jo@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-27 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning demo timing with trace review & travel

Hi Emma —

We can do a limited prompt validation with representative prompts, but having a small workload trace makes the dry-run much higher confidence (helps us validate batching/kv-cache behavior and memory profiles). If you can share a trimmed trace (10–20 example requests) that would be ideal. If not, we’ll proceed with representative traces on our side and flag any risks.

If May 7 at 10:00am PT works for the customer demo, can we lock the internal dry-run for May 6 at 3:00pm PT? Ben will run the environment setup and Marissa will run the runbook checklist.

Pre-dry-run responsibilities (Redwood):
- Provision demo environment with quantization profile and short-lived keys (Ben)
- Validate prompt variants and sample outputs (Monica/Marissa)
- Confirm tracing/logging is enabled and capture a baseline (Marissa)

Pre-dry-run responsibilities (FinLytics):
- Upload finlytics_sample_sanitized.csv to the Drive link and confirm schema
- Provide the small trace_v1.json or an exported sample of requests
- Grant temporary read permissions to demo@redwood-demo (or an equivalent service account)

If that all looks good I’ll send a calendar invitation for both slots once you confirm. I’ve attached our current demo runbook (redwood_demo_runbook_v1.pdf) for your review.

—Monica

Attachment: redwood_demo_runbook_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-27 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning demo timing with trace review & travel

Confirmed — May 6 dry-run at 3:00pm PT and customer demo May 7 at 10:00am PT. I’ll provision the environment and post the service account details in the calendar invite.

- Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Emma Jo <emma.jo@finlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, support@finlytics.com
Date: 2026-04-29 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning demo timing with trace review & travel

Monica —

May 7 at 10:00am PT works for us. We’ve uploaded a sanitized CSV (finlytics_sample_sanitized.csv) to the shared Drive folder and added a small trace export (trace_v1.json). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinLyticsSample.

Ops will create a temporary read-only service account for demo@redwood-demo and share the credentials in the calendar event. We’ll also route a quick signed DocuSign for the data-sharing addendum you requested (link to follow).

Thanks for being flexible — looking forward to the dry-run on May 6.

Best,
Emma

Attachment: finlytics_sample_sanitized.csv (csv), trace_v1.json (json)
